To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

beef, fresh beef and lean beef consumption were associated with higher total energy and protein intake, and increased intakes of sodium, choline, iron, selenium, zinc, phosphorus, vitamin B2, vitamin B3, and vitamin B 6, while fresh lean beef consumption was associated with higher intake of protein and phosphorus only.

beef consumption is associated with an increase of energy, protein, and several vitamins and minerals, and that the association of beef, fresh and lean beef with saturated fat and sodium intake is less pronounced for fresh and lean beef than for total beef consumption

beef, fresh beef and lean beef consumption was associated with higher intakes of protein, choline, iron, selenium, zinc, phosphorus, vitamin B2, vitamin B3, and vitamin B 6, while fresh beef and lean and fresh lean beef were associated with higher intake of vitamin B12 and lower intakes of saturated fats, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between beef consumption and diet quality.
the effects of beef, fresh and lean beef consumption on nutrient intake, diet quality, and health among American adults.
the effects of the consumption of fresh and lean cuts of beef on the diet quality of American adults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consumption of fresh and lean cuts of beef, as part of a healthy and balanced diet, can provide important nutrients for good health.
the study results indicate that beef consumption is associated with a number of nutritional benefits, and that these benefits may be increased by consuming more fresh and/or lean beef.
beef consumption is a significant source of nutrients, and beef consumers are encouraged to increase their share in fresh and lean beef consumption over total beef consumption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the study found that beef consumption, including lean beef, is associated with better nutrient intakes and higher diet quality in U.S. adults, and that fresh and lean beef may be particularly important for nutrient adequacy in U.S. diets.
the consumption of fresh and lean cuts of beef is associated with higher intakes of protein, iron, selenium, vitamin B3, vitamin B12, and zinc.

beef consumption is associated with increased intake of nutrients and diet quality, and beef consumers are advised to choose leaner beef cuts in an effort to minimize the increase in saturated fat intake.
The main takeaway from our work is that
beef consumption, particularly consumption of lean beef and fresh beef, is associated with better diet quality and increased intakes of several important nutrients among U.S. Adults
beef consumption is associated with a higher intake of nutrients of public health concern.
beef is an excellent source of protein, vitamins, and minerals.
